51099567.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to Keap1 Kelch domain (unknown origin) by surface plasmon resonance assay
51099567.references_previous: Jain, A. D.; Potteti, H.; Richardson, B. G.; Kingsley, L.; Luciano, J. P.; Ryujoji, A. F.; Lee, H.; Krunic, A.; Mescar, A. D.; Reddy, S. P.; Moore, T. W. Probing the structural requirements of non-electrophilic naphthalene-based Nrf2 activators. Eur. J. Med. Chem. 2015, 103, 252–268.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Surface Plasmon Resonance Assay. Surface plasmon resonance assays were performed as previously described.1 Briefly, the Kelch domain of KEAP1 was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip. Increasing concentrations of compound solutions were applied to the protein-bound chip, and response units were measured. The experiments were conducted in triplicate with a technical repeat. Approximately 40% of captured KEAP1 was active based on the comparison between calculated RUmax and achieved RUmax: analyte binding capacity (RUmax) = (analyte MW / ligand MW) × immobilization level (RU) One-site binding saturation curves were fitted to the data using GraphPad Prism 6.1.
original_paragraph.Table 1: Table 1. IC50 and Kd Values* *IC50 values, shown in nM units with 95% confidence intervals, were determined by fluorescence anisotropy. Kd values, shown in nM units ± standard deviation, were determined by surface plasmon resonance. aFluorescent interference from 15 impeded accurate determination of IC50. bIC50 and Kd values reported in Jain et al.1 ND = not determined.
original_paragraph.Figure 3 caption: Figure 3. HaCaT cells were treated with 10 μM compound (6a, 6b, 17, 23; positive control CDDO-Im) or vehicle (DMSO) for 6 h (A) or 24 h (D) as shown in the immunoblots. Cell lysates were prepared, equal amount of protein was probed with antibodies specific for NRF2, NQO1, or GCLM. GAPDH was used as a reference. Quantification of band intensities of NRF2 (B, E), NQO1 (C, F), and GCLM levels (G) are shown. DMSO-treated sample values were used as one arbitrary unit. *p < 0.05; **p < 0.01; ***p < 0.001; if no * is indicated, p > 0.05.
original_paragraph.Figure 4 caption: Figure 4. Effects of nonelectrophilic activators 17 (orange) and 23 (purple) and positive control CDDO-Im on the nuclear accumulation of NRF2 in HaCaT Cells. (A) HaCaT cells were treated with DMSO (vehicle) or indicated compound (10 μM) for 6 and 24 h, and cytosolic (C) and nuclear (N) fractions were prepared, and equal amount of protein was immunoblotted using antibodies specific for NRF2. β-Actin/Lamin A/C was used as loading control. (B) Quantification of Nrf2 band intensity using β-actin as reference. DMSO-treated sample value was used as one arbitrary unit. Error bars represent the standard error from four independent experiments. *p < 0.05; **p < 0.01; ***p < 0.001; if no * is indicated, p > 0.05.
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Figure 5. Effects of nonelectrophilic activators 17 (orange) and 23 (purple) on NRF2 target gene expression in HaCaT Cells. (A) HaCaT cells were treated with DMSO (vehicle) or indicated compound (10 μM) for 6 and 24 h. cDNA were prepared from mRNA and analyzed for the target gene expression (A, HMOX1; B, NQO1; C, GCLC; D, GCLM; E, SOD2) using qPCR with specific primers. Relative fold change was calculated with β-actin as reference. DMSO-treated sample value was used as one unit. Error bars represent the standard error from 3 to 4 independent samples. *p < 0.05; **p < 0.01; ***p < 0.001; if no * is indicated, p > 0.05.
original_paragraph.Figure 6 caption: Figure 6. Stability to liver microsomes. Compounds were incubated with mouse liver microsomes (A) and human liver microsomes (B) for 20 min. Percentage of compound remaining after incubation was determined by LC–MS.
